steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Binary form has two sections (A-B); ternary has three (A-B-A) — the return of A in ternary creates a satisfying sense of completion.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Rondo form features a recurring refrain (A) alternating with contrasting episodes (A-B-A-C-A-D-A) — common in Classical concertos.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Sonata form has three sections: exposition (two contrasting themes), development (themes manipulated), recapitulation (themes return in tonic).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Popular music structures: verse-chorus (alternating storytelling and hook), 12-bar blues (I-IV-V chord pattern), intro-outro-break (framing and variation).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe how structure and form are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use structure and form. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use structure and form in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A detailed description using precise musical vocabulary (e.g. specific terms from the AQA elements list), referencing a named piece with accurate observations about how the elements are used and their | A comparison of two pieces identifying similarities and differences in how structure and form are used, explaining the different effects created in each musical context, using comparative language. | A practical application showing understanding of how structure and form can be manipulated in composition or performance, with specific examples of choices made and their intended effect.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use PRECISE musical vocabulary — not vague descriptions like it sounds nice Reference SPECIFIC musical elements when analysing any piece For listening questions: identify elements FIRST, then explain their effect For study pieces: know the context, structure and key features in detail For performing: focus on accuracy, expression and interpretation For composing: show development of ideas, not just repetition
